findings.evidence: The changed text at line 104 correctly says github-issue-creator now has `Edit(issues/**), Read`, but the same component still says at lines 82-83 that invoking it reaches the creator's own bare `Write` access to `issues/`. The old grant description was not updated consistently.
findings.remediation: Update lines 82-83 to describe the scoped `Edit(issues/**), Read` grant, or remove the obsolete sentence; keep the grant description consistent throughout the component and its mirrored copy.

findings.evidence: Workflow 1 can invoke collaborating-on-a-pr when the closing PR has not been created. collaborating-on-a-pr's Path A invokes create-pr, while create-pr's open-issues check can invoke github-issue-lifecycle again. The documents contain explicit stop/skip gates, so this is a gated-only cycle rather than an asserted execution-time recursion.
findings.remediation: Break the cycle by having github-issue-lifecycle stop delegating PR linking to collaborating-on-a-pr, or make the hand-off mutually exclusive with create-pr's github-issue-lifecycle open-issues dispatch and require a separate user-gated invocation that cannot nest.

findings.evidence: The changed allowed-tools entries use Bash(python */analysis-kit/scripts/<script>.py:*). The components' own documentation records that an inline Python code string placed before a matching script path executes under this grant, and that this is a separate write route; mining-review-learnings also grants a fetcher whose --fixture-file accepts an arbitrary local path while its process only uses --pr/--repo.
findings.remediation: Narrow each allowed-tools grant to a mechanically pinned interpreter/script invocation or wrapper that rejects extra code/options and validates paths; remove the unused arbitrary --fixture-file route or expose only a fixed fixture directory.

findings.evidence: The persistence instructions explicitly state that the final report and THIRD_PARTY_REVIEW_LEARNINGS.md diff may contain names, emails, and user paths, while the described redaction only removes secret-shaped patterns.
findings.remediation: Add an explicit pre-sharing/pre-commit redaction warning and require review or removal of names, emails, and local paths before distribution.

findings.evidence: The persistence instructions state that the report may retain names, emails, or user paths from PR review history and transcripts; only secret-shaped patterns are stripped.
findings.remediation: Add a clear redaction-before-sharing/pre-commit instruction covering names, emails, and local paths.

findings.evidence: The report persistence text says secret redaction does not remove personal data and that persisted reports may carry names, emails, or user paths.
findings.remediation: Add an explicit instruction to inspect and redact names, emails, and user paths before sharing or committing the report.
